title: Function Health Lab Weekly Population Percentile Trend
dataSources: HRV (`hrv:reading`), blood oxygen (`spo2:reading`), lab panels (`bloodpanel:result`), supplements (`supplement:intake`), continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), sleep-apnea events (`apnea:event`), body composition (`bodycomp:measure`), blood pressure (`bloodpressure:reading`).
app: Biohacking data — HRV straps, pulse oximeters, blood-pressure cuffs, continuous glucose monitors, body-composition scales, lab-result exports, and supplement logs — ingested to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=function:lab percentile=*
| bin _time span=1w
| stats avg(percentile) as avg_duration, max(percentile) as worst_duration by _time
| sort _time
description: Trends the average and worst population percentile for Function Health lab events each week.
value: Weekly timing trends show whether a process is becoming slower, more erratic, or healthier over time.
implementation: Capture percentile on each event and review weekly averages plus worst cases during your personal ops review.
visualization: Line chart of weekly average population percentile with markers for the worst week.
grandmaExplanation: It times whether Function Health lab tasks are taking longer than they used to and where the slow weeks were.
